purpose:
Appendix E: stage C and stage D of one trial at r = 7, expanded into their totals (standard library only).
Run:  python3 stage_cd.py      prints S_C = 253,143,956,421,123 and S_D = 106,846,183,041,913 and asserts them.

which fix the per-kernel charges in the tables PASS and K3 below (butterfly 3 field operations or 2 when the twiddle is 1, twiddle load with
address, 8 operations per radix-3 leaf, loop control 3 per iteration and 2 on exit). Everything else is a finite recurrence:
  stage C: transform sizes 3*2^a >= 2m-1 and >= m+1; Newton levels l -> min(2l, m-1); the exponent: 224 squaring steps, 45 of them with the multiplication by S;

  stage D: the outer loop of the Euclid driver, hgcd(k) with k halved (rounded up) until k <= 96, in each level the two recursive calls,
           apply_inv (one bilinear convolution), the division by a quotient of degree one, the 2x2 matrix product (conv_bilin_cost);
  below k <= 96 and n <= 192: classical division steps with quotient of two coefficients (divrem_naive).
`Tr` accumulates the operations and the number of live arrays (an allocation is charged 121 + 13 (2 live + 1), a free 105).

name: sep test
purpose:
Join lever check for the BLAKE3 2-round parent node (grid cell basextech / mode / join).

f(L, R) = compress(IV, L || R, t=0, len=64, flags=PARENT|ROOT=12, rounds=2), 256-bit digest.
L, R are the two child CVs (8 words each).  A list / k-list (Wagner) join on f needs output bits that split
as g(L) (+) h(R).  For such a bit the second-order derivative
    D = f(L,R) ^ f(L',R) ^ f(L,R') ^ f(L',R')                   (XOR form)
    A = f(L,R) - f(L',R) - f(L,R') + f(L',R')  mod 2^32          (modular-add form, per word)
is identically 0.  Parts (all against a compression cross-checked with hash-smash/verifier/blake3.py):
  T1 random      L, L', R, R' uniform; per-bit P(D=1) over N quadruples (all 256 bits)
  T2 add         same quadruples, per-bit P(A bit = 1) and P(A word == 0)
  T3 word-pairs  L, L' differ only in word i, R, R' only in word j (64 pairs): a join over 2^32 x 2^32
                 sub-lists would need separability on that subspace
  T4 bit-pairs   L' = L ^ (1<<k in word i), R' = R ^ (1<<l in word j), k,l in {0,7,15,31} (1024 pairs):
                 low-weight differences, where 2 rounds might not have mixed L into R yet
Flag rule: |P - 1/2| >= 2^-8 and z >= Bonferroni threshold; every flagged cell is re-measured on fresh
samples (16x) and counted only if it survives.  Usage: sep_test.py LOGN [seed] -> prints, writes sep.json

purpose:
Exact check-count facts for the sphere door (k of out0,2,5,7 held) in the word-level GD model.

LEMMA (DERIVED; brute-force checked in lemma.py): in the GD model (each equation solvable for any one unknown),
  min checks = min number of equations whose deletion leaves a hypergraph with an EMPTY 2-core
  (2-core = what remains after repeatedly removing a word that lies in exactly one remaining equation, together
  with that equation; guesses are NOT removed - they play no role).
  Proof sketch: in a 0-check order every equation solves a word that occurs in no earlier equation; the last
  core equation cannot do that, because each of its words lies in another (earlier) core equation.  Conversely
  an empty core gives the order (reverse peeling) and the guesses are the words never solved.
  So: non-empty core => at least 1 check, for EVERY guess set.

TABLE MODEL (permissive): any subset B of the live equations of ONE G call (every call treated as table-able,
  the held out-equations of that call allowed in B) may be removed when B has a perfect matching onto words that
  occur in no other live equation.  A real table step (or one of ../gd_promote.py's cycle macros) with 0 checks
  has such a matching (Hall: otherwise a subset of its equations over-determines its words = a check), so a
  non-empty permissive core => at least 1 check with any per-call tables.

Usage: python cores.py [maxdel]     (writes nothing; print to stdout)

purpose:
DDS middle placement: achievable collision probability through chi5 + digest round (COMPUTED, linear algebra).

Given chi5 input difference a5, the chi5 output difference b5 is uniform on the affine space S(a5) (dim w(a5)).
The digest collides when every plane-0 chi6 row has an allowed input difference.  Relaxation used here
(sufficient, so it gives an ACHIEVABLE probability, i.e. an upper bound on the cost):

  then each plane-0 row with only its x=4 bit set costs 2 conditions (PD = 8/32);

Total over the b4 choices of a mid:  P = 2^-(w3+w4) * sum_b4 2^-C_ub(L(b4)).

name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 4-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r4, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one block: chaining value IV, counter 0, length 64,
flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 4 rounds with the message permutation.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian digest integer; the walk is on
g(x) = f(x) XOR q, q the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit (the planes are fed back as the circuit
stores them); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n.
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane recovery circuit (rolled), 3 bit-sliced generator, 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and
recovery, 7 organizer experiments, 8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its text;
everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

purpose:
Our own Orchard PoseidonHash<ConstantLength<2>> (P128Pow5T3, Pallas base field) with a round-prefix parameter.

t=3, rate 2, capacity 1, S-box x^5, R_F=8 (rounds 0-3, 60-63), R_P=56 (rounds 4-59), 64 rounds.
Round i: state += RC[i]; S-box (all 3 lanes if full, lane 0 if partial); state = MDS * state.
Hash: init [m0, m1, 2^65], one permutation, digest = state[0]. No feed-forward.
Constants come from constants_own.py, generated from the PUBLIC halo2_poseidon-0.2.0 fp.rs (gen_constants.py).
Written independently; the PR 923 program was used only as DATA for cross-checking (see check_pr_constants.py).

Op counting (cost rule: one modular add or mult incl. squaring = 1 primitive):
  sbox  = 2 squarings (x^2, x^4) + 1 mult (x^5)        -> 3 mults (2 of them squarings)
  ARK   = 1 add per lane
  MDS   = 3 mults + 2 adds per output lane
Counter keeps add, sqr, mul separately (mul = non-squaring mults); mults_total = sqr + mul.

purpose:

theta_lo = (D - SMAX) / N <= P(next fresh value is a DP | any history of at most SMAX values)

table overflow: Chernoff on Binomial(S, theta_hi) at mcap + 1 must be <= e^-TAB.

name: lane bound
purpose:
Largest lane value of every SUM of the two-stage batch of pkg6, per part, for ALL inputs, by interval arithmetic.

The self-test of the program reports the largest lane of a sum that occurred in its random cases. This tool runs
the same function packed_batch of experiments/halfsearch.py on a second machine that holds, for every register,
not a value but an upper bound of its lanes, and so gives a bound that holds for every context and every member:

  - a loaded word whose lanes are below 2^32 (a constant of the batch, a list word) counts as 2^32 - 1 in every

  - a sum is bounded by the sum of the bounds of its operands;
  - an XOR is bounded bit by bit: below 2^32 it can be anything, above bit 31 it has at most the bits that one of
    the operands can have;
  - an AND with a loaded constant is bounded by the largest lane of that constant, a shift by 2^36 - 1 (bits of the

  - an OR is bounded by the all-ones word of the longer operand.

largest bound of all, and the largest bound of a word that enters the flag computation (it must be below 2^32).

    e1 = Y3 + y, e1' = Y3' + y, h1' = h1 ^ eta,

breadth-first search over the bits of h1, low to high, checking each condition bit as soon as all the bits it reads

name: ---- partitions (8 chunks of 16 bits) ----
purpose:
Period-4 class decomposition and rotation-adapted coordinates of the front-line residual (rotational lens).

Sets (each n x 4 u32, word order = digest words 1,3,4,6):
  R   residual (data/res.u32)
  RP  rotational coordinates (R1, R3, U4 = R4 ^ ROR(R1,8), U6 = R6 ^ ROR(R3,8)); a bijective GF(2)-linear map of R
  SH  control: R with each word column independently permuted (keeps one-word marginals, breaks cross-word links)
  U   control: uniform random words
Every number is computed separately on half T (train, first half of rows) and half V (test, second half).

Measures:
 1. Class bytes: word w, class c = bits {c, c+4, ..., c+28} packed into 8 bits. Plug-in Shannon entropy with the
    Miller-Madow correction, and P(byte = 0); the same for contiguous bytes.
 2. 16-bit chunk partitions of the 128 bits (8 chunks): sum of chunk entropies = an estimate of an upper bound on
    H(R) (subadditivity); deficit = 128 - sum. Class-based, contiguous and 24 random partitions (selection control).
 3. Class words: class c over all four words (32 bits): Renyi-2 entropy from collision pairs; zero count.
 4. Rotation filtration: per word, w mod (x+1)^m (m = 1..16) in the Pascal basis a_k = parity(w & S_k),
    S_k = {i : i AND k == k}; these quotients commute with every rotation and with XOR. Compared with the m low bits.
 5. Period-4 distance d4 (distance to the nearest nibble-repeated word) per word.

name: affine
purpose:
affine.py: can small-t cube members be ENUMERATED instead of filtered? (a push on the method's size limit)

Per outer step the map F: c1 -> t (the counter solved from E1.d1 = c1 - Y11) is a bijection built from three
rotations (16, 7, 8: net ROR 1), XORs with constants and four additions of constants. Over the T1 cube (11 fixed
bits, 21 free bits) it is close to affine over GF(2). The affine-guided enumerator:
  1. evaluate F at the cube's base point and at base XOR e_i for the 21 free bits: delta_i = F(base^e_i)^F(base)
     (22 evaluations, about 300 word ops);
  2. solve over GF(2): bits >= k of F(base) ^ sum x_i delta_i must be 0 (32 - k equations, 21 unknowns);
     inconsistent -> skip the outer step;
  3. enumerate the solution space (particular + null space), compute F exactly on each candidate, keep t < 2^k.
Ground truth: all t in [1, 2^k) inverted through F^-1 (exact list of cube members with small t).
Reported: fraction of outer steps flagged good vs actually good, recall (true hits found / all true hits),
candidates per hit (exact evaluations per kept trial).

name: heur
purpose:
heur.py  (untried/b3-heur; research only; run inside WSL Ubuntu, one CPU process at a time)

Non-gradient heuristic for the class choice of E3 (layer r1d, free const, counter base): simulated annealing over
ONE member e1 = Y3 + Y4 (Y4 is an outer word on the counter path, so one member is enough), scored by the team's
exact counter tool pair_calc_sub (beta* = 18b0e098 alone, pin H8; the same call as counter_next/stack/run_cube.sh with
-cube ffffffff e1).  Per-member rates (normalisation of scan_y4.py, free = 0):
    total = sum_j L_j N_j / 2^64  over every row      (the objective of the stack's greedy scan; best known 76,161,024)
    S     = the same sum over the six front-line taus  (class value 67,633,152, the map's Section 2.6 figure)
Phase A: e1 inside the front-line class (e1 AND 03cf8303) = 030c0303, 19 free bits, eta = 830303cf.

name: ---- the outcomes and the solver answers
purpose:
Review helper (lens: judge). One thread. Reads evidence/pairs_recount_830303cf.txt and the solver files; writes
review/judge_n3_rule.txt.

An exact count of the E3 side of every outcome, SPLIT BY THE RULE, with an enumeration written for this review from
the definitions of proof 6.2 (no solver, no sampling, integers only). For an outcome (tau, eps):

  N3      = number of (Y4, h1, Y9, w8), Y4 in the class, with f1^f1' = psi, e2^e2' = eps, g2^g2' = tau
  N3_rule = the same with h1 satisfying the rule (4, 5 or 6 conditions)

Uses: (1) N3 against the calculator's N3 of the same outcome (a check of both programs); (2) the 54 answers
"unsatisfiable" behind the count that the claim uses: an outcome has no violating solution exactly when
N3 = N3_rule; (3) the exact rate r_A under M, which the text says "was not computed".

Method. Variables (Y4, h1, g1 = Y9 + h1, e2 = e1 + f1 + w8), a bijection for fixed Y4. psi = tau ^ ROR(tau,1),
gamma = ROL(psi,12), rho = ROR(eta ^ eps, 8).
  C1  g1' = g1 + dh with dh = eta - 2 (h1 & eta); g1 ^ g1' = gamma  <=>  dh = gamma - 2 (g1 & gamma) mod 2^32.
  C2  e2' = e2 + D, D = DY3 + psi - 2 (f1 & psi), f1 = ROR(Y4 ^ g1, 12); (e2 + D) ^ e2 = eps fixes, when it is
      possible at all, the bits of e2 at the positions i < 31 of eps: e2_i = bit i+1 of D ^ eps.
  C3  h2 = ROR(h1 ^ e2, 8), h2' = h2 ^ rho, g2 = g1 + h2, g2' = (g1 ^ gamma) + (h2 ^ rho); g2 ^ g2' = tau: counted by a

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

walsh.c - joint lens: every GF(2) mask of weight 1..4 over the 128 residual bits, with train/test and controls.
  walsh <res.u32> <raw|spiral> <rows> <seed> [maxw]
Coordinates: raw    W = (R1, R3, R4, R6)
             spiral W = (R1, R3, R4 ^ ROR(R1,8), R6 ^ ROR(R3,8) ^ ROR(eta,8))   (a linear bijection of R; RESULT.md s.2)
Data sets (each split into train = first rows/2, test = last rows/2; shuffles act within each half):

name: shapegraph

Exact shape facts (32-bit, no sampling).  Owner: shape_odd agent.
1. call-message graph: each message word links its round-0 call and its round-1 call -> cycle decomposition.
2. lattice symmetries: the 4x4 state is a torus Z4 x Z4 with rows = roles (a,b,c,d), columns and diagonals =
   G lines.  Find every map (r,c) -> (r, e*c + s*r + t) that sends columns to columns and diagonals to
   diagonals, its induced message-word map, whether it commutes with the message permutation, and whether
   it fixes the initial state.
3. Moebius / slide: the unique message M* whose round 0 returns the initial state (one round is a bijection,
   inverse formulas of ../../sol_answer_W_newpaths.md 3.3); then 2-round(M*) == 1-round(P M*).
4. Circle: per-word rotation-invariant sets and the birthday on rotation classes.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one block: chaining value IV, counter 0, length 64, flags 11 =
CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q,
q = the mask of the polarities of the stored digest planes (0 for the rolled program: the planes are stored upright).  n = 256 is the claim; the organizer experiments
run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are renaming; full adders by
the pivot rule), 4 the rolled program (rounds 1-2 straight, rounds 3-7 a loop of one generic round) and its register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and
recovery, 7 organizer experiments, 8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its text; the rest is our program.

event AND satisfies the rule on h1. The GPU programs count this joint event on real trials; the package compares it
only with draws from the model. Here it is counted exactly, with a method written for this purpose.

fixed on the bits of ROL(psi,12) below 31; for each such g1 pattern every member of the class is visited (arrays),

purpose:
Small-field analogue of the line construction: how often does a centre give a usable root?

The claim's premise H_root is about the deployed Orchard Poseidon over the 255-bit Pallas field at degree
5^(6+r) (millions to billions). Nothing here reaches that size. This program builds the SAME CONSTRUCTION on a
toy Poseidon-like permutation over a small prime p (p = 2 mod 5, so x -> x^5 is a bijection): state [nk, rho, cap],
two full rounds, a line in the (U, V) plane that makes round 1 free, L further layers (full and partial rounds),
digest = coordinate 0 after the last MDS. Constants and the 3x3 MDS are drawn from a fixed seed (they are NOT the
deployed constants, whose field is far larger).

has degree exactly D = 5^L by finite differences, (3) for EVERY centre c in F_p decides exactly whether some
s != 0 has F(c+s) = F(c-s) (equivalently, the odd part g_c has a root S = s^2 that is a nonzero square), and
(4) does the same for a uniformly random table as a control. The reported number is the exact fraction of centres,
for that one fixed toy function. It is a measurement on toys. It is not a bound for the deployed target, it is not
a sampled probability, and the seeds are fixed in this file (declared in advance), not taken from the request.

name: split
purpose:
b3-misc/split.py -- cell const x join (GAPS item 5).

Question: can extra constants (one more pinned word, or any set of them) split
the front-line system so that E1's inputs and E3's inputs range independently
(a Cartesian product, so a list join on the 128-bit residual becomes possible)?

Method (word level, structural = generic counting, the guess-and-determine model):
  * Trace the reference 2-round compression (verifier/blake3.py) into word
    relations: each G call = 8 relations (a1=a+b+x, d1=ror(d^a1,16), c1=c+d1,
    b1=ror(b^c1,12), a2=a1+b1+y, d2=ror(d1^a2,8), c2=c1+d2, b2=ror(b1^c2,7)).
    Every relation is solvable for any one of its words given the others.
    The trace is checked against blake3._compress on random inputs.
  * System = round 0 (K0..K3, D0..D3) + round-1 columns (C0..C3).
    Fixed: init state, w4, w13, w14, w15, pins X3, X7, X11, X15; words forced by
    the fixed ones are propagated (so C3 is constant, as in the map).
  * Terminals: E1 inputs {Y1, Y6, Y12, w12, w5}; E3 inputs {Y4, Y9, Y14, w8}
    (Y3, Y11, w15 are constants).
  * A split labels every free word U (E1 side), V (E3 side) or S (constant /
    separator) and every relation U, V or S, with no relation touching both U
    and V. Structural dimensions: d_X = #words_X - #relations_X.
    d_U + d_V + d_S = dim (8 at the root, 9 with t_lo free, 10 with t free).
    The exact optimum over ALL labelings (so over every choice of extra
    constants) is found by an ILP (scipy milp / HiGHS).

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its

name: sep test copy
purpose:
Join lever check for the BLAKE3 2-round parent node (grid cell basextech / mode / join).

f(L, R) = compress(IV, L || R, t=0, len=64, flags=PARENT|ROOT=12, rounds=2), 256-bit digest.
L, R are the two child CVs (8 words each).  A list / k-list (Wagner) join on f needs output bits that split
as g(L) (+) h(R).  For such a bit the second-order derivative
    D = f(L,R) ^ f(L',R) ^ f(L,R') ^ f(L',R')                   (XOR form)
    A = f(L,R) - f(L',R) - f(L,R') + f(L',R')  mod 2^32          (modular-add form, per word)
is identically 0.  Parts (all against a compression cross-checked with hash-smash/verifier/blake3.py):
  T1 random      L, L', R, R' uniform; per-bit P(D=1) over N quadruples (all 256 bits)
  T2 add         same quadruples, per-bit P(A bit = 1) and P(A word == 0)
  T3 word-pairs  L, L' differ only in word i, R, R' only in word j (64 pairs): a join over 2^32 x 2^32
                 sub-lists would need separability on that subspace
  T4 bit-pairs   L' = L ^ (1<<k in word i), R' = R ^ (1<<l in word j), k,l in {0,7,15,31} (1024 pairs):
                 low-weight differences, where 2 rounds might not have mixed L into R yet
Flag rule: |P - 1/2| >= 2^-8 and z >= Bonferroni threshold; every flagged cell is re-measured on fresh
samples (16x) and counted only if it survives.  Usage: sep_test.py LOGN [seed] -> prints, writes sep.json

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its

name: lbsat3
purpose:
Lower bound on the free width of ANY binary join tree (DP over any shape), with promoted constants chosen
freely up to a slack budget S (shape_any agent).  Refines lbsat2.py: the size window counts only equations that
still contain an unknown word after promotion (r_e), as in the propagated sub-family system.

  slack(P) = |P| - E + maxmatch(eq, words \ P) <= S   <=> vertex cover C with |P| + |C| <= S + E   (Konig)
  window   : k <= #{e in A : r_e} < 2k,   r_e = OR_{v in e} not p_v
  cost     : |Y \ P| - #{e in A : vars(e) <= Y u P} <= T,  Y >= B(A) \ P
UNSAT => for every promotion set with slack <= S and every tree on the remaining equations having a node in the
window (true when the remaining system has >= 2k equations; checked by mode 'drop'), width > T.

Usage: python lbsat3.py cut  <sys> <k> <T> <S> <out.cnf>

name: bitgd
purpose:
Bit-level guess-and-determine for a ring subsystem (shape_torus, 2026-10-08).

Each 32-bit word is itself a ring Z/w of bits: a rotation is a shift around that ring, an addition is a carry
chain that runs one way (bit 0 -> bit w-1) and so CUTS the bit ring at bit 0.  A word-level ring closure
f(c) = c can be solved by seeding s bits and running around the bit ring; s is what this module estimates.

Input: word-level primitive equations (name, words) in the gd_order.py format, the set of UNKNOWN words
(everything else is known), word size w.  Roles (from the equation name):
  X:a1 / X:a2  out = in1 + in2 + in3       X:c1 / X:c2  out = in1 + in2
  X:d1 R0, X:b1 R1, X:d2 R2, X:b2 R3       out = ROR_R(in1 ^ in2)
  outN                                     w0 ^ w1 = const
Bit variables: word bits, carry bits, temp-word bits.  Bit equations:
  linear (xor of <= 4 bits = known): solves any one unknown;  carry c[i+1] = MAJ(x_i, y_i, c_i): forward only.
Seeds = guessed bits.  Propagation is exact (each step determines one bit uniquely from known ones), so
"seed s bits, propagate, test the unused equations" enumerates every root with 2^s passes.   [DERIVED]

name: sep test3
purpose:
Join lever check for the BLAKE3 2-round parent node (grid cell basextech / mode / join).

f(L, R) = compress(IV, L || R, t=0, len=64, flags=PARENT|ROOT=12, rounds=3), 256-bit digest.
L, R are the two child CVs (8 words each).  A list / k-list (Wagner) join on f needs output bits that split
as g(L) (+) h(R).  For such a bit the second-order derivative
    D = f(L,R) ^ f(L',R) ^ f(L,R') ^ f(L',R')                   (XOR form)
    A = f(L,R) - f(L',R) - f(L,R') + f(L',R')  mod 2^32          (modular-add form, per word)
is identically 0.  Parts (all against a compression cross-checked with hash-smash/verifier/blake3.py):
  T1 random      L, L', R, R' uniform; per-bit P(D=1) over N quadruples (all 256 bits)
  T2 add         same quadruples, per-bit P(A bit = 1) and P(A word == 0)
  T3 word-pairs  L, L' differ only in word i, R, R' only in word j (64 pairs): a join over 2^32 x 2^32
                 sub-lists would need separability on that subspace
  T4 bit-pairs   L' = L ^ (1<<k in word i), R' = R ^ (1<<l in word j), k,l in {0,7,15,31} (1024 pairs):
                 low-weight differences, where 2 rounds might not have mixed L into R yet
Flag rule: |P - 1/2| >= 2^-8 and z >= Bonferroni threshold; every flagged cell is re-measured on fresh
samples (16x) and counted only if it survives.  Usage: sep_test.py LOGN [seed] -> prints, writes sep.json

purpose:

event AND satisfies the rule on h1. The GPU programs count this joint event on real trials; the package compares it
only with draws from the model. Here it is counted exactly, with a method written for this purpose.

Partial E3 event of a pair (psi, eps): Y4 in the class, and for the words (Y4, h1, Y9, w8)
    f1 XOR f1' = psi   and   e2 XOR e2' = eps        (the first five assignments of E3 for A and B).
With e1 = Y3 + Y4, g1 = Y9 + h1, e2 = e1 + f1 + w8 the map (Y4, h1, Y9, w8) -> (e1, h1, g1, e2) is a bijection, and
    (g1 + dh) XOR g1 = ROL(psi, 12),   dh = (h1 XOR eta) - h1        (a function of the 13 bits of h1 on eta)
    (e2 + D) XOR e2 = eps,              D = DY3 + (f1 XOR psi) - f1,  f1 = ROR(Y4 XOR g1, 12).
For an addition x -> x + D with a prescribed XOR difference X the solutions x form a cube: the carry into bit i is
D_i XOR X_i, so D_0 = X_0, D_(i+1) XOR X_(i+1) = D_i wherever X_i = 0 (i < 31), and x_i = D_(i+1) XOR X_(i+1)
wherever X_i = 1 (i < 31); all other bits of x are free. So: for each of the 2^13 patterns of h1 on eta, g1 is
fixed on the bits of ROL(psi,12) below 31; for each such g1 pattern every member of the class is visited (arrays),
D is formed and the cube of e2 is counted. Nothing is sampled.

The word-level model (gd_order.py) treats each 32-bit word as one unit and needs exactly 4 checks (128 bits) per family
member for the fixed variant.  Here every word is split into its 32 bits, and every modular addition gets its carry
bits.  Structural rules only (no value-dependent shortcuts):

  - carries: k[i+1] = maj(p[i], q[i], k[i]) is known once its three inputs are known (forward only); k[0] = 0.
A three-term addition z = p + q + x uses an intermediate word t = p + q.
checks (in bits) = guessed bits - family freedom in bits.  A member then costs about 2^checks trials.

name: Pallas base field modulus.
purpose:
Organizer-owned byte-message Poseidon reference implementation.

The target is the Poseidon instance deployed in Zcash Orchard: `PoseidonHash`,
the `P128Pow5T3` parameter set over the Pallas base field. Width 3 with rate 2
and capacity 1, S-box x^5, R_F = 8 full rounds (four leading and four
trailing) and R_P = 56 partial rounds between them, so 64 rounds in total.
Each round adds its round constants to all three state elements, applies the
S-box (to every element in a full round, to element 0 only in a partial
round), then multiplies the state by the MDS matrix.

Reduced variants execute rounds 0 through rounds-1 of that fixed deployed
schedule and stop. This is a prefix reduction, so round i always uses row i of
the deployed round constants and the deployed MDS matrix is never regenerated.
Rounds 0 to 3 and 60 to 63 are full; rounds 4 to 59 are partial. Any prefix
from 1 to 64 rounds is supported; the hash mode, initial state, message

element 0. No padding block is ever appended at this length.

strictly less than p. Non-canonical encodings are rejected, because x and
x + p would otherwise encode one field

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 6-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r6, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 6 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).

L1  For a fixed G input (a,b,c,d), the maps (x,y) -> (a2,d2) and (x,y) -> (b2,c2) are bijections.
    Consequence: equal G inputs with a message difference always change BOTH a row-a/d output word

name: neutral
purpose:
Bit-level, basis-free test for cheap E3-holding moves (neutral bits), on the own model (b3.py).
Free input bits: T0, m0 m1 m2 m3 m5 m6 m7 m9 m10 m11 m12 (12 words = 384 bits) and, for counter 2, T1 bits 0..18.
Held: pins X3 X7 X11 X15 and E3 inputs Y4 Y9 Y14 (224 bits); m4 m13 m8 m14 m15 are constants (no difference).
XOR-linear model: every modular addition replaced by XOR (rotations and XORs are exact).  A move delta keeps every held

k-list merge (Wagner k-tree, many solutions) on random lists, mixed xor / modular-add coordinates.

Toy group G = product of c coordinates of w bits, each 'add' (Z/2^w) or 'xor' ((Z/2)^w).  n = c*w.

Cost counted in element-steps: build (leaf elements computed), ins (table inserts), look (streamed lookups),
out (elements produced at every join node, root outputs = solutions).  Predicted = the same recursion on

name: count-cost e3rule
purpose:
count-cost reviewer: the exact probability, under the seven-word model, that a trial shows a listed partial E3
event AND satisfies the rule on h1. The GPU programs count this joint event on real trials; the package compares it
only with draws from the model. Here it is counted exactly, with a method written for this purpose.

Partial E3 event of a pair (psi, eps): Y4 in the class, and for the words (Y4, h1, Y9, w8)
    f1 XOR f1' = psi   and   e2 XOR e2' = eps        (the first five assignments of E3 for A and B).
With e1 = Y3 + Y4, g1 = Y9 + h1, e2 = e1 + f1 + w8 the map (Y4, h1, Y9, w8) -> (e1, h1, g1, e2) is a bijection, and
    (g1 + dh) XOR g1 = ROL(psi, 12),   dh = (h1 XOR eta) - h1        (a function of the 13 bits of h1 on eta)
    (e2 + D) XOR e2 = eps,              D = DY3 + (f1 XOR psi) - f1,  f1 = ROR(Y4 XOR g1, 12).
For an addition x -> x + D with a prescribed XOR difference X the solutions x form a cube: the carry into bit i is
D_i XOR X_i, so D_0 = X_0, D_(i+1) XOR X_(i+1) = D_i wherever X_i = 0 (i < 31), and x_i = D_(i+1) XOR X_(i+1)
wherever X_i = 1 (i < 31); all other bits of x are free. So: for each of the 2^13 patterns of h1 on eta, g1 is
fixed on the bits of ROL(psi,12) below 31; for each such g1 pattern every member of the class is visited (arrays),
D is formed and the cube of e2 is counted. Nothing is sampled.

The claim's premise H_root is about the deployed Orchard Poseidon over the 255-bit Pallas field at degree

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its

name: e3split
purpose:
e3split.py (counter_next/knobs; research only): a cheaper exact E3 search by splitting h1 at bit 12.

The bits of h1 below 12 reach the rest of E3 only through (i) the carry pair into bit 12 of g1 = Y9 + h1 and
g1' = Y9 + h1', (ii) g1 bits 0..11 (-> f1 bits 20..31 -> e2 bits 20..31), (iii) h1 bits 8..11 (-> h2 bits 0..3)
and (iv) g1 bits 0..11 in g2 = g1 + h2.  e2 bits 0..19 depend only on f1 bits 0..19 = (y ^ g1) bits 12..31 and
start with carry 0.  So, per target:
  LOW : all h1 bits 0..11 meeting dg1 bits 0..11, grouped by the carry pair into bit 12 (bit-serial search);
  HIGH: for each carry pair present, all h1 bits 12..31 meeting dg1 bits 12..31 and de2 bits 0..19 (bit-serial);
  JOIN: every (low, high) pair with the same carry pair -> full check of the four E3 differences.
Cost = nodes of LOW + nodes of HIGH + number of JOIN pairs (each a full E3 evaluation, about 30 operations).
Checked against e3dfs.search (plain search, itself checked against the 2^32 brute force) on planted and random
outer steps.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

name: exact routes
purpose:
Exact linear-consistency filter for word-level message-only routes (one process, capped).

The truncated model (trunc_search.c) treats every cancellation as possible.  Here every word also
carries its modular difference as a linear form over GF(p) (p = 2^61-1, a proxy for the integers):
  - message word m_j: its own variable (the SAME variable in round 0 and round 1);
  - an addition: the exact sum of its input forms; a cancellation adds the constraint "sum = 0";
  - an xor-rotate output: a fresh variable (no linear relation assumed: optimistic);
  - every active value must stay nonzero (not forced to 0 by the constraints).
A route is linearly infeasible when the constraints force an active value to 0.

Refined round-1 cost (model B'): xor cancellations and fold cancellations count 1; an addition
cancellation counts 1 when its reduced constraint involves a fresh variable (a condition on values),
0 when it only relates message differences (a free choice of differences) or is already implied.

Search: depth-first over the 16 G calls and all op-level cancellation choices, pruned by the exact
truncated model-B cost-to-go (round-0 conditions free, round-1 + fold counted) and by linear
infeasibility.  So it is exhaustive over routes whose truncated model-B cost is <= budget.

  python -B exact_routes.py <M> <budget> [node_cap]

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one block: chaining value IV, counter 0, length 64, flags 11 =
CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q,
q = the mask of the polarities of the stored digest planes (0 for the rolled program: the planes are stored upright).  n = 256 is the claim; the organizer experiments
run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are renaming; full adders by
the pivot rule), 4 the rolled program (rounds 1-2 straight, rounds 3-7 a loop of one generic round) and its register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and
recovery, 7 organizer experiments, 8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its text; the rest is our program.

name: oclib
purpose:
Ones'-complement lens (Z/(2^32-1)) on the front-line residual: shared counting and evaluation.

Counts are built either in numpy (from the stored data) or by oc_stream.c (streaming, fresh samples); both
produce the SAME flat layout (layout() below), so one evaluator serves both.

Quantities, per residual word w in (1,3,4,6) (index 0..3):
  D  = oc(dA) - oc(dB) mod M          the residual read in ones'-complement coordinates (primary)
  R  = oc(dA ^ dB)                     the XOR residual R read as an element of Z/M
  E  = D - oc_diff(x) - oc_diff(y)     epsilon: what is left when D is split as E1 part + E3 part
                                       (digest word = x ^ y, x from one diagonal G, y from the other)
  S  = oc(dA) - oc(dA ^ R_other) mod M surrogate: D rebuilt with a residual from ANOTHER row (keeps R's
                                       distribution, breaks the dA <-> R coupling); a control, never tested
where oc(x) = x mod (2^32-1) (0xFFFFFFFF -> 0) and M = 2^32-1 = 3*5*17*257*65537.

name: pair free
purpose:
pair_free.py - universal price of one matched pair in the last step.

Two G calls P (plays G4 or G5) and Q (plays G6 or G7) with FREE input differences in all four
rows and (option) free message differences. The collision condition on their digest words is
out(P) = (c,d,a,b) of out(Q), i.e. P.a2=Q.c2, P.b2=Q.d2, P.c2=Q.a2, P.d2=Q.b2.  Q's output must be
nonzero (in every route that cancels inside round 0, some last-step call has a nonzero b/c
input, so by lemma L1 its output is nonzero).  Minimises LM weight of P plus Q.
Any 2-round characteristic whose last step contains such an active pair costs at least this.

usage: pair_free.py --W N --out runs/NAME [--msg free|zero] [--rows abcd|ac|bd]

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 5-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r5, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one block: chaining value IV, counter 0, length 64, flags 11 =
CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 5 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q,
q = the mask of the polarities of the stored digest planes (0 for the rolled program: the planes are stored upright).  n = 256 is the claim; the organizer experiments
run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are renaming; full adders by
the pivot rule), 4 the rolled program (rounds 1-2 straight, rounds 3-5 a loop of one generic round) and its register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and
recovery, 7 organizer experiments, 8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its text; the rest is our program.

name: site scan
purpose:
Own code (blake3-r3 dig, units U61-U63).  Exhaustive scan over all 2^32 values of ONE initial-state word v_i (i in 0..11),
every other initial word standard (IV, counter 0, length 64, flags 11) or given by argv.  Round 0 column calls C0..C3 read the
zero key words m0..m7, so they are pure functions of the initial state; the four diagonal calls D0..D3 then add / xor those

  D3=G(3,4,9,14):  p3+p4, p14, p9, p4
For v_i in column j = i mod 4 only p_j, p_{j+4}, p_{j+8}, p_{j+12} change.  Output: for each of the 16 sites the number of
values of v_i that make the site constant 0, the histogram of the number of zero sites, and the first solutions.

name: entropy bound
purpose:
Joint lens: upper bounds on the Shannon entropy of R in several coordinate systems (all are linear bijections of R).
Chow-Liu bound over the 16 aligned bytes: H(R) <= sum_i H(b_i) - sum_{edges of a spanning tree} I(b_i; b_j)
(chain rule with each byte conditioned only on its tree parent). The tree is the maximum-MI spanning tree chosen on the
TRAIN half; the bound is evaluated on the TEST half. Entropies are plug-in with the Miller-Madow correction.
Also: collision entropy H2 of each 32-bit coordinate word from the full 2^20 rows (single words; sums are a GUESS
of the joint H2 under independence of the words).
Coordinates:  raw     (R1, R3, R4, R6)
              spiral8 (R1, R3, U3 = R4^ROR(R1,8), U1 = R6^ROR(R3,8)^ROR(eta,8))
              spiral7 (R1, R3, Z7 = R4^ROR(R1,7), Q7 = R6^ROR(R3,7))
              mixed   (R1, R3, Z7, U1)
Control: uniform words, same count (raw coordinates).
Run: python entropy_bound.py > entropy_bound_out.txt

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its

purpose:

Audit step 3: table rules.

    family constants; enumerate all 256 values of the target, propagate plainly from constants + triggers + target and
    count the values consistent with every fully known equation.  Valid rule: the true value is always consistent.

Part 2a: own word-level model of the 55/63 construction and own basis test (no SAT, no team code).

Model: every G assignment is one equation over the unknown words it contains; each equation can be solved
for any one of its unknowns (all are bijective in each argument).  E1/E3 first halves are modelled with the
pinned Y11, Y3, w15 substituted (c1 = Y11 + d1, e1 = Y3 + Y4).  Constants: IV, block length, flags, the pins

Counter: K0's d input is v12 = T0, K1's d input is v13 = T1; COUNTER=0: both constant 0; 1: T0 unknown;
2: T0 and T1 unknown.

Basis test.  B (|B| = n - m) is a triangular basis iff forward propagation from B determines every word.
Existence of a basis containing a forced set F is decided by REVERSE PEELING: repeatedly delete an equation
that owns a word not in F occurring in no other remaining equation.  Peeling is monotone (a private word stays
private when other equations are deleted), so greedy peeling succeeds iff some order does (proof in
STRUCTURE.md); success <=> a basis containing F exists, and the peeling gives the order (reversed) and the
basis (unclaimed words).  validate() checks this against brute force on random small systems.

E1 side. In the cube, c1b = c1 ^ CM (beta = beta*), and d2b = d2 ^ ror(tau, 8). So
    eps = (c1 + d2) ^ ((c1 ^ CM) + (d2 ^ ror(tau, 8)))
depends on (c1, d2) only. For each listed tau of beta*, count (c1 in the cube, d2 any 32-bit value) with eps = eps*,
split by the parities c1[11]^c1[12] and c1[20]^c1[22]. Every d2 value is reachable by some a2, so a zero count
means NO trial (any a1, Y6, w5, outer words) can give the listed E1 outcome in that cell.

E3 side. h1b = h1 ^ ETA (class), so Delta g1 = (y9 + h1) ^ (y9 + (h1 ^ ETA)) depends on (y9, h1) only, and the
listed partial E3 events of eps* need Delta f1 = ror(Delta g1, 12) in the eps* list. Count (y9, h1) per value of
(y9[0], y9[1], y9[2]); a zero count means no outer step with those Y9 bits can give such an event.

name: ---------------- GF(2) helpers ----------------
purpose:
XOR-linearised 2-round BLAKE3 (toy width w) for collision-characteristic search with the output fold.

Model (DERIVED, standard: Chabaud-Joux linearisation; Su et al. 2010 and GKNWW14 sec. 6 use it on BLAKE/BLAKE2):
  every modular addition is replaced by XOR; a characteristic is then a linear function of the input
  difference (message difference dM, 16w bits, plus a block-length difference dv14 in the low LW bits).
  Each 2-input addition with input XOR differences (p, q) is passed (output p^q) with probability
  2^-hw((p|q) & ~MSB) (Lipmaa-Moriai, xdp+ for gamma = p^q).  A 3-input add a+b+x is scored as the best of the
  three evaluation orders: min over pairs hw(p|q) + hw((p^q)|r), MSB excluded.
  Collision: dout_i = dv_i ^ dv_{i+8} = 0 for all 8 output words (the fold is part of the linear map).
Positions: one per non-MSB bit of every addition input word.

name: Toy run of Algorithm 6 (Dong et al. 2021, MITM partial-target -> collision).
purpose:
Toy run of Algorithm 6 (Dong et al. 2021, MITM partial-target -> collision).
w=4-bit cells, h=8 cells (32-bit output), t=m=4 cells (16-bit target, matched exactly),
DoF+ = DoF- = 4 cells (16 bits each side). Paper eq 9 (table terms dropped) predicts
(2^4)^(8/2 - min{4-2,4-2,4-2,2}) = 2^8 work.  Constrained bound predicts ~2^(w(h+t)/4)=2^12

Episode = fresh random F,G,R (new gray constants). Forward list: L random x, key F(x);
backward: L random y, key G(y); match F(x)==G(y) (target cells = 0); each match is a
partial-target preimage, costs 1 evaluation of the remaining 16 output bits R(x,y);
birthday on R across all episodes. Cost = list elements + matches, until first collision.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

purpose:
Largest lane value of every SUM of the two-stage batch of pkg6, per part, for ALL inputs, by interval arithmetic.

The self-test of the program reports the largest lane of a sum that occurred in its random cases. This tool runs
the same function packed_batch of experiments/halfsearch.py on a second machine that holds, for every register,
not a value but an upper bound of its lanes, and so gives a bound that holds for every context and every member:

  - a loaded word whose lanes are below 2^32 (a constant of the batch, a list word) counts as 2^32 - 1 in every
    lane, whatever its value; the word "bit 32" and the two counters are taken as they are;
  - a sum is bounded by the sum of the bounds of its operands;
  - an XOR is bounded bit by bit: below 2^32 it can be anything, above bit 31 it has at most the bits that one of
    the operands can have;
  - an AND with a loaded constant is bounded by the largest lane of that constant, a shift by 2^36 - 1 (bits of the
    neighbouring lane come in; every shift of the batch is followed by an AND with a loaded mask);
  - an OR is bounded by the all-ones word of the longer operand.

It prints, per part, the largest bound of a sum in units of 2^32 next to the bound of the program's TABLE, the
largest bound of all, and the largest bound of a word that enters the flag computation (it must be below 2^32).
It then runs the program's own machine on random batches and checks that every sum that occurs is at most the

V5  R_0 = x^p mod g, R_i = R_(i-1) o R_(i-1) mod g, Q = x^(p^L) mod g by the binary chain; g_L = gcd(g, Q - x), g_1 = gcd(g, R_0 - x);

purpose:
e3cond.py (counter_next/stack; research only)

The E3 side of a counter-arrangement trial, written as three exact XOR-difference conditions on one inner word.

Per outer step the counter arrangement fixes y = Y4, Q = Y9, W = w8 (Sol answer Y section 7: E3 coordinates (y,Q,W,h));
only h1 moves.  With E = Y3 + y + w8 and E' = Y3' + y + w8 = E + DY3 (exact), and E1 outcome (beta, tau, eps):
  R = 0  <=>  dE3.c = tau (word 1), dE3.a = eps (word 3), dE3.b = ROR(tau,8) (word 4), dE3.d = ROR(beta^eps,7) (word 6)
and with h1' = h1 ^ eta (class), f1 = ROR(y ^ g1, 12), e2 = E + f1, h2 = ROR(h1 ^ e2, 8), g2 = g1 + h2:
  (1) (Q + h1) ^ (Q + (h1 ^ eta)) = G   with G = ROL(tau ^ ROR(tau,1), 12)          [from words 1 and 4]
  (2) (E + f1) ^ (E' + (f1 ^ ROR(G,12))) = eps                                       [word 3]
  (3) (g1 + h2) ^ (g1' + h2') = tau,  h2 ^ h2' = ROR(eta ^ eps, 8)                   [word 1]
  word 6 needs n = eps ^ ROL(beta ^ eps, 1) ^ eta = 0 (Lemma N; E1 only).
Part A checks these identities on random real E3 executions (both messages).  Part B counts, exactly by carry DP over
one 32-bit word, the solutions of (1) for sampled Q and of (2) for sampled E, for the seven beta* outcomes, and the share

purpose:
s3-2block-capacity / origin_test.py
Question: in a 2-block message, block-1 sets block-2's 512 capacity bits (chosen at cost ~2^c for c linear
conditions). Does a nonzero/chosen capacity enlarge the rounds-affine field for block 2, or deepen it
(2-round -> 3-round), relative to the single-block capacity=0 case?

Math being tested: affinity of a round map on a direction-span is governed by the SECOND finite difference
(cube sum over a pair of directions) = the polarization. For a degree-<=2 map this is a CONSTANT, independent
of the base point. The capacity is part of the base point. So capacity cannot change affinity of any map that
is degree<=2 on the field. W40 makes rounds 0-1 affine, so F2 is degree 2 and F3 = chi3 o affine is degree 2
on W40 -> origin-independent. This script verifies it on the organizer round function (cd.rnd, verified vs
keccak.py by cd.selfcheck).

Outputs per round depth k=1..4:
  - affine_defect_rank: GF(2) rank of the set of 2nd differences {D_wi D_wj F_k} over W40 pairs
    (0 => F_k is affine on all of W40; >0 => not affine, max affine subspace is smaller).
  - cap_variant_mismatches: number of pairs whose 2nd difference DIFFERS between capacity=0 and a
    random capacity base (and a second random base). 0 => capacity provably irrelevant at this depth.
Control: random SOURCE directions outside W40 (chi1 already quadratic) -> F3 2nd diff SHOULD depend on capacity.
Usage: python origin_test.py SEED NPAIRS

name: model
purpose:
Part 2a: own word-level model of the 55/63 construction and own basis test (no SAT, no team code).

Model: every G assignment is one equation over the unknown words it contains; each equation can be solved
for any one of its unknowns (all are bijective in each argument).  E1/E3 first halves are modelled with the
pinned Y11, Y3, w15 substituted (c1 = Y11 + d1, e1 = Y3 + Y4).  Constants: IV, block length, flags, the pins
X3 X7 X11 X15 w4 w13 w15 (and w14 unless --w14free), hence all of K2's first four values and C3 entirely.
Counter: K0's d input is v12 = T0, K1's d input is v13 = T1; COUNTER=0: both constant 0; 1: T0 unknown;
2: T0 and T1 unknown.

Basis test.  B (|B| = n - m) is a triangular basis iff forward propagation from B determines every word.
Existence of a basis containing a forced set F is decided by REVERSE PEELING: repeatedly delete an equation
that owns a word not in F occurring in no other remaining equation.  Peeling is monotone (a private word stays
private when other equations are deleted), so greedy peeling succeeds iff some order does (proof in
STRUCTURE.md); success <=> a basis containing F exists, and the peeling gives the order (reversed) and the
basis (unclaimed words).  validate() checks this against brute force on random small systems.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its

sizecap.py: the method's size limit. What the counter lever is worth when the message length is capped.

A cap of L bytes means t <= (L - 63) / 1024, i.e. t < 2^k. Two ways to meet it (32-bit real arithmetic):

  I (invert): per outer step, run every t < 2^k backwards through the bijection t -> c1 (about 14 word ops)
     and keep the c1 that fall in the T1 cube.

  outer step, for k = 12..32), and the same count by inversion for k = 12; spread across outer steps.
Part 2 (DERIVED, the one formula of counter\adjudicate\adj_check.py with ops GUESSES):
  time_log2 = 84.96 + log2(cost per kept trial / 6.5), against the filed 92.53.
  F: cost = 11 * 2^(32-k) + 6.5 (11 ops to reach t, GUESS); I: cost = (OUTER + 14 * 2^k) * 2^(11-k) + 6.5
  (OUTER = 400 ops per outer step, the census GUESS).

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,

claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).

renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).

For every G call and every subset Q of its 8 primitive equations: W = non-constant words of Q.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

name: struct split
purpose:
ctr x join, part S: structural (word-level) split search over EVERY triangular basis.

Uses the equation system of counter_next/knobs/model.py unchanged (imported).
A triangular basis = an orientation of the equations (each equation solves one of its words),
acyclic, every non-basis word solved exactly once.  With up to `max_checks` equations left
unsolved (checks), the basis grows by that many words.

Targets (from coupling.py diffs(), checked in RESULT.md):
  key1 (E1 side, 128 bits) is a function of T1 = {E1.a2, E1.b1, E1.d1}
  key3 (E3 side, 128 bits) is a function of T3 = {E3.h1, E3.g1, E3.f1, E3.e2}

Split (meet-in-the-middle) = a triangular basis B = U + V + Fx with
  T1 depending on no V word, T3 depending on no U word,
  T1 depending on some U word, T3 depending on some V word.
Then for each Fx, key1 = f(U) and key3 = g(V): a list join decouples the two sides.
With checks allowed, a check equation must contain no word that depends on both U and V
(so it is separable and can be joined on); gain needs min(|U|-cU, |V|-cV) > cX.

Dependency is structural (union over the solving equation's other words); a structural
non-dependency is an exact non-dependency.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

name: ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

purpose:
construction_drat.py -- independent reviewer, lens "construction", part (d): proofs for the 54 answers "no solution".

The count that H1 uses keeps 54 outcomes because solvers answered that the E3 system has no solution that violates
rule A. The package says these answers have no certificate. Here, for each of the 54:

  1. the reviewer's formula (construction_rule.build, question 2) is solved by cadical in plain mode (no
     preprocessing, so every learned clause follows by unit propagation) with a text DRAT proof;
  2. the proof is checked by a forward checker written here: every added clause must give a conflict by unit
     propagation from its negation (RUP), deletions are ignored (sound for RUP), and the empty clause must be reached;
  3. drat-trim is used as well if it is installed.

Before that the encoding itself is tested: for random inputs, unit propagation on the two G calls of the formula must
assign every variable and give the eight values of both calls as plain arithmetic does (so the formula excludes no true
execution on these inputs), and the three clauses of "h1 violates rule A" are checked on all 64 patterns of the six
bits. Runs in WSL: python3 -B construction_drat.py [workers=3] [minutes=8].

purpose:
Review helper (lens: judge). One thread. Reads evidence/pairs_recount_830303cf.txt and the solver files; writes
review/judge_n3_rule.txt.

An exact count of the E3 side of every outcome, SPLIT BY THE RULE, with an enumeration written for this review from
the definitions of proof 6.2 (no solver, no sampling, integers only). For an outcome (tau, eps):

  N3      = number of (Y4, h1, Y9, w8), Y4 in the class, with f1^f1' = psi, e2^e2' = eps, g2^g2' = tau
  N3_rule = the same with h1 satisfying the rule (4, 5 or 6 conditions)

Uses: (1) N3 against the calculator's N3 of the same outcome (a check of both programs); (2) the 54 answers
"unsatisfiable" behind the count that the claim uses: an outcome has no violating solution exactly when
N3 = N3_rule; (3) the exact rate r_A under M, which the text says "was not computed".

Method. Variables (Y4, h1, g1 = Y9 + h1, e2 = e1 + f1 + w8), a bijection for fixed Y4. psi = tau ^ ROR(tau,1),
gamma = ROL(psi,12), rho = ROR(eta ^ eps, 8).
  C1  g1' = g1 + dh with dh = eta - 2 (h1 & eta); g1 ^ g1' = gamma  <=>  dh = gamma - 2 (g1 & gamma) mod 2^32.

      possible at all, the bits of e2 at the positions i < 31 of eps: e2_i = bit i+1 of D ^ eps.
  C3  h2 = ROR(h1 ^ e2, 8), h2' = h2 ^ rho, g2 = g1 + h2, g2' = (g1 ^ gamma) + (h2 ^ rho); g2 ^ g2' = tau: counted by a

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its
text; everything else is our 0a9640ed / 3356413f program.

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its

name: -------- 1 scalar digest
purpose:
Birthday collision search on 7-round BLAKE3-256 (blake3-r7, one block) with 256 bit-sliced lanes and distinguished points.

The message is 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes (words m0..m7) and x (words m8..m15, little endian), one chunk of one block: chaining value IV, counter 0,
length 64, flags 11 = CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT, 7 rounds with the message permutation between rounds.  f(x) is the 256-bit little-endian
digest integer; the walk is on g(x) = f(x) XOR q, where q is the fixed 256-bit mask of the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit
(the digest planes are fed back as the circuit stores them, no complement is computed); g(x) = g(y) if and only if f(x) = f(y).  n = 256 is the
claim; the organizer experiments run the same code at reduced n (the low n bits of g).
Sections: 1 scalar digest, 2 packed 7-lane tracer (the recovery circuit), 3 bit-sliced generator (256 lanes, one plane per bit: rotations are
renaming; full adders by the pivot rule), 4 register allocation, 5 plan and ledger, 6 search and recovery, 7 organizer experiments,
8 command line (--selftest --ledger --loss --sweep --stats --gen-c), 9 the circuit generator in C (GEN_C).
Credit: the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q are the method of jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (proof 3.3, 3.4), implemented here from its

purpose:
outer_filter.py [OUTCOMES]   (counter_next/stack; research only)

EXACT share of outer steps that can contain a collision, for the counter arrangement (pin H8, 55/63, sub-class).
Per outer step the E3 inputs y = Y4, Q = Y9, W = w8 are fixed (only h1 moves); E = Y3 + y + w8, E' = E + DY3.
For an E1 outcome (beta, tau, eps) with n = 0, an E3 match needs (e3cond.py, checked on 200,000 real pairs):
  (1) exists h1:  (Q + h1) ^ (Q + (h1 ^ eta)) = G(tau),  G = ROL(tau ^ ROR(tau,1), 12)
  (2) exists f1:  (E + f1) ^ (E' + (f1 ^ ROR(G,12))) = eps
Both are properties of outer words only.  An outer step where, for every listed outcome, (1) or (2) has no solution
holds no trial with R = 0 of a listed outcome: skipping it loses no collision (exact, no model).
Counted exactly over all 2^32 Q and all 2^32 E by subset-construction DPs (state: the reachable carry pairs of the
existential word, per outcome).  Q and E are independent uniform words under M_outer (Sol answer Y section 7: Q = Y9 and
W = w8 are two of the seven independent outer words; E = Y3 + y + W), so
  P(pass) = sum over (solvable pattern a of Q, solvable pattern b of E) P(a) P(b) [a and b share an outcome].
OUTCOMES: 'bstar' (the 7 rows of beta*, default) or 'all' (every row of a15_outcomes.tsv with a nonzero product).

name: count-cost e3rule
purpose:
count-cost reviewer: the exact probability, under the seven-word model, that a trial shows a listed partial E3
event AND satisfies the rule on h1. The GPU programs count this joint event on real trials; the package compares it
only with draws from the model. Here it is counted exactly, with a method written for this purpose.

    python -B count-cost_e3rule.py            (Windows Python with numpy; one thread; about a minute)

Partial E3 event of a pair (psi, eps): Y4 in the class, and for the words (Y4, h1, Y9, w8)
    f1 XOR f1' = psi   and   e2 XOR e2' = eps        (the first five assignments of E3 for A and B).
With e1 = Y3 + Y4, g1 = Y9 + h1, e2 = e1 + f1 + w8 the map (Y4, h1, Y9, w8) -> (e1, h1, g1, e2) is a bijection, and
    (g1 + dh) XOR g1 = ROL(psi, 12),   dh = (h1 XOR eta) - h1        (a function of the 13 bits of h1 on eta)
    (e2 + D) XOR e2 = eps,              D = DY3 + (f1 XOR psi) - f1,  f1 = ROR(Y4 XOR g1, 12).
For an addition x -> x + D with a prescribed XOR difference X the solutions x form a cube: the carry into bit i is
D_i XOR X_i, so D_0 = X_0, D_(i+1) XOR X_(i+1) = D_i wherever X_i = 0 (i < 31), and x_i = D_(i+1) XOR X_(i+1)
wherever X_i = 1 (i < 31); all other bits of x are free. So: for each of the 2^13 patterns of h1 on eta, g1 is
fixed on the bits of ROL(psi,12) below 31; for each such g1 pattern every member of the class is visited (arrays),
D is formed and the cube of e2 is counted. Nothing is sampled.

Checks: the cube rule against brute force

name: ---------- pure-python references for the self-test ----------
purpose:
xplus1 lens library: the ring GF(2)[x]/(x^32+1) = GF(2)[x]/((x+1)^32).

A u32 word w is the polynomial sum w_i x^i.  Rotation left by r = multiplication by x^r (a unit),
XOR = ring addition.  Write w = sum_j c_j (x+1)^j.  By Lucas, C(i,j) is odd iff j is a bit-subset of i,
so c_j = XOR of w_i over all i that are bit-supersets of j.  `digits(w)` returns the word whose bit j is c_j
(a superset-sum Moebius transform on the 5-bit index; it is an involution).

valuation v(w) = min{ j : c_j = 1 } (32 for w = 0).  Ideal I_k = ((x+1)^k) = { v >= k }, dimension 32-k.
I_{32-2^s} = words of period 2^s (I_28 = period-4 words).  w mod (x+1)^(2^s) = XOR-fold of w to 2^s bits.
